newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open little changed Tuesday as traders expect the market to consolidate gains racked up during the previous session.
Monday, benchmark July ended up 0.16 cent at 11.04 cents a lb after trading from 11.08 to 10.89 cents. The rest settled 0.17 to 0.05 cent higher.
Market sources attributed gains to mostly technical factors. An early move over resistance at 10.95 cents in July triggered buy stops, sending the contract to key 11.00 cents.

But talk that Cargill has found a buyer for nearly 360,000 tonnes of sugar, coupled with rumors that some of the Brazilian origin is from the new crop, lent some support to the market, trading sources said.
Resistance was now seen at 11.09 cents, the recent high hit on April 30, followed by 11.20 cents for July sugar.

In London, white sugar futures followed through on the previous day's gains early Tuesday, amid continued fears of seasonal tightness. Benchmark LIFFE August rose 40 cents as of 0854 EDT/1354 GMT, to $317.00, just off the intraday high of $317.40. The back months were up $0.20 to $1.10.
